input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The async wrapper's shared statistics dict is cleared on each call and shared between concurrent invocations.
- rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather runs several calls of the same @retry async function. Mechanism: each call clears the dict and the copies write into the same one, so counters interleave. Impact: statistics are corrupted, and a call that has already started loses its counters.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is shared, each call clears it, and concurrent calls (asyncio.gather) overwrite each other's counters, including the start state of a call already in progress. It covers only the async path, but that path is part of the labeled failure.
